mechanism: Claim-evidence entailment graph with uncertainty-weighted contradiction detection
origin_domain: computational argumentation and natural language inference
inputs: set of atomic claims extracted from a text or record
metadata about source provenance and timestamps
transformation: An AI model decomposes inputs into atomic propositions, maps each proposition to supporting or refuting passages, assigns calibrated entailment, contradiction, or insufficiency scores, and builds a graph where edges represent evidential dependency or conflict.
constraints: AI inference must be central to proposition extraction and entailment scoring
outputs must remain traceable to source spans
low-confidence or missing-evidence claims must be explicitly marked
the mechanism is independent of any particular audience or interface

mechanism: Content lineage anchoring with selective disclosure proofs
transformation: Each state transition in a content lifecycle is hashed and linked to prior states, then committed to a blockchain or append-only ledger. Zero-knowledge or selective disclosure proofs allow verification of specific attributes without revealing all metadata.
constraints: cryptographic anchoring must be material to the provenance path
private metadata must not be exposed unless explicitly disclosed
verification must not require trusting the original storage location
hash collisions and key compromise require defined failure handling

mechanism: Constraint-aware generative search over candidate policies
transformation: An AI search process proposes candidate policies, evaluates them against a simulator or learned outcome model, rejects infeasible candidates using constraint checks, and iteratively improves candidates using reward signals and counterexample feedback.
constraints: AI-driven search or policy generation must be core to the mechanism
hard constraints must be enforced separately from reward optimization
outputs must include feasibility evidence, not only scores
simulation error must be represented in uncertainty estimates

mechanism: Multimodal deviation detector with causal hypothesis ranking
transformation: AI encoders convert heterogeneous signals into comparable latent representations, detect deviations from learned baselines, correlate anomalies across modalities, and rank candidate causal hypotheses using temporal ordering and intervention-aware counterfactual checks.
constraints: AI representation learning must be central to fusing heterogeneous inputs
detected anomalies must be compared against an explicit baseline
causal hypotheses must be presented as ranked estimates rather than facts
counterfactual estimates must expose assumptions and uncertainty
